correctness.rationale: The Schur complement with each 2x2 Hermitian peripheral block yields the polynomial identity for all complex z after polynomial extension; regrouping equal strengths supplies a monic quotient. Evaluating at each positive distinct strength has a provably nonzero denominator and gives each class cosine sum, including degeneracy boundaries. Two closed 3-step paths prove each local rooted moment. Six independent exact symbolic cases, a phase-degenerate explicit pair and 240 seeded floating-point configurations corroborate the identities. No finite computation is presented as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The unweighted friendship graph spectrum is one special zero-flux equal-weight parameter point; it does not imply inverse identifiability with independently adjustable fluxes. The general cospectrality trace criterion can be applied to this model but contains no class-by-class recovery theorem or the local repair statement. Prior common-flux transport scattering fixes the same phase in every petal and likewise cannot infer arbitrary per-petal flux cosines.

value.rationale: Independent magnetic phases are natural physical controls in tight-binding loop networks; isospectral ambiguity matters for recovering local gauge flux from global spectroscopy. The theorem gives a complete infinite-family identifiability classification with a constructive inverse and a sharp physical remedy: local third-order return moments separate fluxes hidden by repeated bond magnitudes. Unlike a generic determinant identity, the result establishes exactly what information global and site-resolved measurements recover and shows a genuine non-gauge-equivalent ambiguity.
